import.title: Data sources and import
import.intro: Upload official export files. Files stay on this machine (data/imports); we never ask for or store passwords.
import.uploaded: Upload complete, the import has started.
import.noProfiles: No profiles were found in the export.

hint.imdb_ratings: On IMDb, open “Your Ratings” and pick “Export” from the menu at the top right. Download the CSV when it's ready and upload it here.
hint.imdb_watchlist: On IMDb, open your watchlist and choose “Export this list”. Upload the downloaded CSV here.
hint.netflix_export: Netflix account → Security & privacy → “Download your personal information”. The ZIP usually arrives by email within a few days; upload it as is, without unzipping.
hint.prime_video_export: Amazon → Account → Data & privacy → “Request your data” → Prime Video. The ZIP (“Prime Video.zip”) usually arrives within a few days; upload it as is, without unzipping. The export only separates the adult (ADULT) and child (CHILD) profile types; trailers and promos do not count as watched.

unsupported.disney_plus_export: You can get your Disney+ watch history through a GDPR data request, but there's no automatic import for it yet. Until then, mark titles you've watched with “Seen it” on the cards.
unsupported.hbo_max_export: You can get your HBO Max watch history through a GDPR data request, but there's no automatic import for it yet. Until then, mark titles you've watched with “Seen it” on the cards.
unsupported.apple_tv_export: You can get your Apple TV+ watch history through a GDPR data request, but there's no automatic import for it yet. Until then, mark titles you've watched with “Seen it” on the cards.
unsupported.skyshowtime_export: You can get your SkyShowtime watch history through a GDPR data request, but there's no automatic import for it yet. Until then, mark titles you've watched with “Seen it” on the cards.

import.unsupportedGeneric: You can get your {provider} watch history through a GDPR data request, but there's no automatic import for that format yet. Until then, mark titles you've watched with “Seen it” on the cards.
import.assignHint: Pick an app profile for each export profile; one upload can import into several profiles.

library.title: Household exports
library.intro: Exports uploaded by any profile of the household. You can import any of them into your own profile; the viewing data always stays with the profile you import it into.
library.fileMissing: The file is no longer on the server; upload it again.

settings.title: Settings
settings.dataSourcesHint: Upload IMDb ratings, your IMDb watchlist and the Netflix data export, and see what's not possible yet for the other services.
settings.languageHint: Language of the interface and of the chat's answers.

refresh.title: Catalog refresh
refresh.hint: Fetches availability changes, new arrivals and notifications. This can take up to a minute.

auto.title: Automatic refresh
auto.days: At least every N days (0 = off)
auto.hint: The server refreshes by itself once the interval since the last successful run has passed; a due run waits for the preferred hour.

env.title: Diagnostics
env.hint: Read-only status from the backend; secret values are never shown.

secrets.title: API keys
secrets.hint: Keys are stored locally in the server's .env file and are never sent back to the browser – you only see whether each one is set (and its last 4 characters).

secrets.invalidTmdb: TMDB rejected this key. Make sure you pasted the API key (v3).
secrets.lmStudioUrlHelp: Address of your local LM Studio OpenAI-compatible server. Don't expose it publicly.

backup.name: File
backup.restoreHint: Choose an earlier .db backup and inspect it first; restoring is only possible after that.
backup.confirmBody: The current database will be replaced entirely by the selected backup. A safety copy of the current state is made automatically first, but changes made since the backup will be gone from the active database.
backup.previousBackup: Safety copy of the previous database
